notes:
High-volume chat deflection focus — cost-first evaluation.

Key metrics / ask:
- Typical traffic: ~1.3M customer messages/day (API messages), ~15M tokens/day after context.
- Peak concurrency: ~1,200 active sessions during promo spikes.
- Target latency: p95 < 750ms for short-turn chat, p50 ~150-200ms desirable.
- Cost sensitivity: finance wants unit economics <= $0.0009/token (end-to-end).
- Model preference: open/quantized Llama-style large model family acceptable; want recommendations for q4_0/q8_0 profiles to meet cost targets.
- Reliability ask: graceful degradation — fallback to smaller model or cached replies during overload.

POC notes (internal):
- Ran batching knob sweep (batch sizes 8/16/32) — saw 18-26% token cost reduction at batch=16 with 12% latency tail increase.
- Prefix/KV caching reduced repeated-context tokens by ~22% for routine FAQ flows. Need deeper session-level cache TTL analysis.
- Tried quantized 4-bit (q4) variant: CPU decode latency up ~12% but unit cost drop ~38% vs FP16 on same infra. Ops flagged interest in hybrid (dedicated GPU + quantized fallback).

Security / procurement quotes:
- "Need proof we can keep EU customer data in-region; also must show audit_log retention 1 year." — VP Ops
- "If we can hit the unit cost target, we'll consolidate ~60% of live chat to SiftWave flows." — Head of CX

Open technical risks / asks for Redwood team:
- Provide modeled unit-cost spreadsheet (tokens, batching, cache hit rates) with sensitivity to prefix lengths.
- Run controlled spike test (1k -> 1.5k concurrent sessions) and capture p50/p95/p99 across routes.
- SOC2 evidence for Dedicated offering + KM integration guide (HSM/KMS).
